body.message: What loudness does Spotify normalize to?

response.reply: Spotify normalizes to -14 LUFS integrated on its default "Normal" setting (Spotify Support, Critical Listening Lab, Trackgleam, Soundcamps). For the best results, they recommend keeping your True Peak below -2 dBTP to avoid distortion during encoding (Spotify Support).

results.title: Loudness normalization on Spotify
results.snippet: If your master is louder than -14dB integrated LUFS, keep True Peak below -2dB to avoid extra distortion. Louder tracks are more susceptible to extra distortion when encoded for streaming. These guidelines also apply to tracks delivered for lossless playback.

results.title: Spotify Loudness Standard — Target LUFS & Normalization
results.snippet: With normalization on, Normal targets -14 LUFS; Premium listeners can also choose Loud (-11 LUFS) or Quiet (-19 LUFS). In Normal mode, quieter tracks can receive positive gain within available peak headroom. Loud mode uses a limiter.

results.title: Streaming Loudness Targets 2026 — Spotify, Apple Music LUFS ...
results.snippet: The 2026 mastering loudness reference chart: every streaming platform's LUFS and true-peak target in one table. Spotify -14 LUFS, Apple Music -16 LUFS, YouTube, Tidal, Amazon and more.

results.title: Spotify LUFS Analysis: How Loud Your Mix Should Be in 2026
results.snippet: Apr 7, 2026 · Spotify measures your track's integrated LUFS (loudness over the full duration of the file) and compares it to a target level. On the default "Normal" playback setting, that target is -14 LUFS.
